title: Chapter 6 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of semantic HTML, landmarks, and web accessibility!

questions.question: Why is semantic HTML important for accessibility?
options: It makes the code run faster
It helps assistive technologies understand the page structure
questions.explanation: Semantic elements have implicit roles that screen readers use to navigate content.

questions.question: Which element is used for the main navigation block of a site?
questions.explanation: <nav> semantically denotes navigation.

questions.question: You can have multiple `<header>` elements on a single page.
questions.explanation: Yes, each article, section, or the page itself can have its own header.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `<main>` element?
options: To contain the unique, primary content of the page
questions.explanation: <main> holds the dominant content distinct from repeated elements like headers and footers.

questions.question: Which element is appropriate for a sidebar with related links?
questions.explanation: <aside> is for tangentially related content, like a sidebar.

questions.question: What does the `<article>` element represent?
options: A self-contained composition that could be independently distributed
questions.explanation: <article> is a self-contained piece of content like a blog post or comment.

questions.question: Which attribute should you add to `<time>` to provide a machine-readable date?
questions.explanation: The `datetime` attribute holds the standard format (YYYY-MM-DD).

questions.question: The `<address>` element is for any physical address on the page.
questions.explanation: It is specifically for contact information of the page/article author.

questions.question: What is the four-letter acronym for the WCAG principles?
questions.explanation: POUR stands for Perceivable, Operable, Understandable, Robust.

questions.question: Which WCAG conformance level should you aim for to meet legal and accessibility standards?
questions.explanation: Level AA is the generally accepted target for most websites.

questions.question: Why is keyboard navigation important?
options: Many assistive technologies and users rely solely on keyboard
questions.explanation: Keyboard accessibility ensures users with motor impairments can operate the site.

questions.question: Removing the focus outline (outline: none) is fine if it doesn't match your design.
questions.explanation: You must provide a custom, visible focus indicator; removing it without replacement breaks accessibility.

questions.question: What is the minimum colour contrast ratio for normal text (WCAG AA)?
questions.explanation: WCAG AA requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for standard text.

questions.question: What does ARIA stand for?
questions.explanation: ARIA stands for Accessible Rich Internet Applications.

questions.question: When should you use an ARIA role instead of a native HTML element?
options: Always, because ARIA is more modern
Only when there's no native HTML element that conveys the correct semantics
questions.explanation: The first rule of ARIA: don't use ARIA if a native element does the job.

questions.question: The `aria-label` attribute provides an accessible ______ for an element.
questions.explanation: `aria-label` defines the accessible name for assistive technology.

questions.question: What does `aria-live="polite"` do?
options: Makes the element visible only to screen readers
Announces content changes to screen readers without interrupting the user
Prevents the element from being focused
questions.explanation: `aria-live` regions inform assistive technology about dynamic content changes.

questions.question: How can you test basic keyboard accessibility?
options: Unplug the mouse and navigate using Tab and Enter
questions.explanation: Keyboard‑only testing reveals focus order and reachability issues.

questions.question: Which tag creates a 'skip to main content' link target?
questions.explanation: The target can be `<main id="main-content">` and the link `href="#main-content"`.

questions.question: Using semantic HTML eliminates the need for ARIA entirely.
questions.explanation: Semantic HTML covers many cases, but complex widgets may still need ARIA to convey states (e.g., tabs, modals).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a landmark element?
questions.explanation: <div> is a generic container without implicit landmark role.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of a 'skip to content' link?
options: It allows keyboard users to bypass repetitive navigation
It hides content from screen readers
questions.explanation: Skip links let users jump directly to the main content, avoiding tabbing through every nav item.
